To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
resistance training is an effective way to prevent falls in older adults, and that resistance training is a safe way to improve strength in older adults.

the effects of resistance training on strength, muscle mass, and functional mobility in elderly individuals were greater when resistance training was performed at high intensity and with a large range of motion than when it was performed at low intensity and with a small range of motion.

(a) maximal strength training with elastic bands is an effective method for improving strength and function in older adults, (b) maximal strength training is effective in improving functional mobility in older women, (c) maximal isometric strength training with elastic band is an effective method to improve functional mobility in older men, and (d) maximal isokinetic resistance strength training is an effective method of improving strength and functional mobility of older women.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of strength training on functional mobility in older people.
the effects of maximal resistance training on strength, functional mobility, muscle activation and muscle architecture in older adults.
the effects of maximal resistance training on strength gains, muscle hypertrophy and functional mobility in the elderly.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
maximal isometric resistance training is more effective than maximal isokinetic training in increasing strength in older adults.
resistance training is an effective intervention for the elderly to increase muscle strength.
the evidence is not sufficient to recommend either isometric or isokinetic training for improving muscle strength or functional mobility in older persons.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the effects of maximal resistance training on strength, power, and function in older adults are positive.
resistance training is an important component of an overall exercise program for older adults.
we have demonstrated the effectiveness of a resistance exercise program on the improvement of functional mobility in older people.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the effects of resistance training on strength, muscle mass, and functional mobility are similar regardless of the type of resistance training performed.
resistance training is a very effective way to prevent falls in older people and improve mobility, strength and balance.
older adults can gain strength and improve functional mobility through a combination of maximal isometric resistance training and maximal isokinetic resistance.
